name: Blackjack
description: Blackjack (also known as 21) is the most iconic casino banking game in the world. Players compete individually against the dealer to reach a hand value as close to 21 as possible without exceeding it (busting). Known for its combination of chance and mathematical strategy, it is the only casino game where a skilled player can systematically gain an edge over the house through basic strategy and card counting.

history.origins: Descended from the 17th-century French game 'Vingt-et-Un' (Twenty-One). The name 'Blackjack' originated in American gambling halls that offered a special 10-to-1 payout for an Ace of Spades and a black Jack (Spades or Clubs).
timeline: 1700s: Vingt-et-Un is played in French courts and casinos.
1800s: Brought to the United States; rules evolve into the modern banking format.
1962: Edward O. Thorp publishes 'Beat the Dealer', proving that card counting can overcome the house edge.
Present: The standard for casino table games worldwide and a massive online gaming staple.
history.cultural: A symbol of the high-stakes casino environment, famously featured in countless films and literature as the ultimate game of skill vs. house.
history.evolution: The game moved from single-deck play to multi-deck 'shoes' and automated shuffling machines to counter strategic card counting.

setup.players: Typically 1 to 7 players seated at a semi-circular table, all playing against a central Dealer.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card French decks (usually 6 or 8 decks in a shoe).
setup.dealing: After bets are placed, players and the dealer receive two cards each. Usually, one of the dealer's cards is face up (upcard) and one is face down (hole card).
setup.equipment: Casino table, chips, card shoe, discard tray.

rules.objective: Achieve a hand value closer to 21 than the dealer's hand, without exceeding 21.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Wagering**: Players place bets. 2. **Deal**: Players and dealer receive two cards. 3. **Player Turn**: Players choose to 'Hit' (take card), 'Stand' (keep hand), 'Double Down' (double bet for one card), or 'Split' (split pairs). 4. **Dealer Turn**: Dealer reveals hole card and must hit until reaching 17+. 5. **Settlement**: Higher hand wins; dealer bust pays all remaining players.
keyRules: Face cards (K, Q, J) count as 10.
Insurance is offered if the dealer's upcard is an Ace.

strategy.basic: Follow the 'Basic Strategy' chart: always hit on 11 or less, always stand on hard 17 or more. Stand on 12-16 if the dealer shows a 2-6 (bust cards).
strategy.intermediate: Double Down Timing: Always double down on a total of 11 unless the dealer shows an Ace. Double on 10 against a dealer 2-9.
strategy.advanced: Card Counting: Use the Hi-Lo system to track the ratio of high cards (10s, Aces) to low cards. Increase your bet when the 'True Count' is positive, as this increases the probability of a player blackjack.
tips: Never take insurance; it is a 'sucker bet' with a high house edge.
Avoid 6-to-5 payout tables; always look for traditional 3-to-2 blackjack payouts.

synthesis.shortDescription: The world's most popular casino game. Take your seat at the table, place your bet, and test your nerves against the dealer. Whether you're playing basic strategy or counting cards, the goal is simple: get closer to 21 without going over. Double down on 11 and pray for an Ace!
